dish.title: Taiwanese Lu Rou Fan: Braised Pork Belly over Rice with Soy Eggs and Bok Choy
dish.description: Diced skinless pork belly browned with golden shallots and garlic, then braised in soy sauce, dark soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, brown sugar, and five-spice with peeled boiled eggs until glossy and tender, spooned over short-grain rice with garlicky baby bok choy.

recipe_version.title: Taiwanese Lu Rou Fan: Braised Pork Belly over Rice with Soy Eggs and Bok Choy
recipe_version.description: Diced skinless pork belly browned with golden shallots and garlic, then braised in soy sauce, dark soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, brown sugar, and five-spice with peeled boiled eggs until glossy and tender, spooned over short-grain rice with garlicky baby bok choy.

ingredients.name: dark soy sauce
ingredients.display_name: dark soy sauce whose label lists water, soybeans, wheat, salt, and sugar

ingredients.name: Shaoxing wine
ingredients.display_name: Shaoxing wine whose label lists water, glutinous rice, wheat, and salt

steps.title: Prep
steps.body: Dice the pork belly, slice the shallots, mince the garlic, halve the bok choy, and rinse the rice until clear.

steps.title: Boil the eggs
steps.body: While you cook the shallots and pork (overlap stated): bring 4 cups water to a boil in a 2-quart saucepan over high, about 6 minutes to come to a boil. Lower in the eggs, simmer 9 minutes, cool under the cold tap 2 minutes, and peel.

steps.title: Golden shallots
steps.body: Heat 1 tbsp oil in the 5.5-quart Dutch oven over medium, about 1 minute. Cook the shallots, stirring, until golden, about 7 minutes. Lift out half with the slotted spoon and set aside.

steps.title: Brown the pork
steps.body: Add the pork to the pot and cook, stirring, until the fat renders and the edges brown, about 8 minutes. Stir in 6 cloves of garlic for 1 minute.

steps.title: Braise
steps.body: Add the soy sauce, dark soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, brown sugar, five-spice, 2 cups water, the reserved shallots, and the peeled eggs. Bring to a boil, cover, and braise on low, turning the eggs now and then, until the pork is very tender, about 50 minutes. Uncover and simmer until glossy and lightly sticky, about 8 minutes.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.body: During the braise (overlap stated): combine the rice and 1 3/4 cups water in the lidded 2-quart saucepan, bring to a boil over high, about 4 minutes, cover, turn to low, and cook 15 minutes. Rest covered off the heat 10 minutes.

steps.title: Bok choy and serve
steps.body: Heat 1 tbsp oil in the 12-inch skillet over medium-high, add the remaining garlic and the bok choy, then 2 tbsp water and the salt. Cover and steam until tender-crisp, about 3 minutes. Spoon pork and sauce over bowls of rice, add a halved egg and bok choy.

coverage_contribution: Taiwanese meals in the catalog are beef noodle soup and three-cup mushrooms; there is no braised pork rice bowl. A slow comfort pork dinner.
near_duplicate_review: Compared with cantonese-char-siu-pork-rice: diced pork belly braised soft in soy and five-spice, not roasted glazed pork slices. Compared with taiwanese-beef-noodle-soup: a saucy pork rice bowl, not a beef noodle soup. Compared with japanese-gyudon: slow-braised pork belly with eggs, not quick-simmered sliced beef.
not_duplicate_of: Not Chinese red-braised pork belly (finely diced, served over rice with eggs) and not chashu.
